en: That stainless reality which the wise declare to be beyond even the intellect and the self-born [Brahmā].

Salutations to You, the Lord of the Daughter of the Snowy Mountain (Himavat), for the welfare of embodied beings; You who, though consisting of the universe, have Your manifold divisions perceived as merely adventitious (aupādhika); and who, within the body, describe the sequence of one's own sleeping consciousness through the nature of mantra. 1. May the Lord, adorned with the crescent moon as his ornament, generate bliss in your hearts—he by whom the entirety of the three worlds is sustained through some indescribable portion of his splendor. (2)

Salutations to those venerable sandals, by performing prostrations before which even once, men who were sinking in the waves of the ocean of saṃsāra cross over it with their minds’ darkness destroyed. (3)

May those particles of dust from the lotus feet of the Guru—who are honored by all the world, who are respectfully borne upon the heads of all yogis once they are liberated from the objects of sense that have been burnt away by the fire of knowledge—nourish the clarity of your minds. (4)
I have neither the unrestrained eloquence of speech nor the skill of intellect; indeed, I am not capable of understanding the reality of the auspicious Buddha.
